fixes.row: Who is saved: “everyone”, “the world”, “all Israel”; “a few”, “the remnant”, “the chosen”
fixes.why: The label gives the universal side first. The note says ‘in the Bible’s order’, but the heading still reads the question in one direction, which rule 2 forbids. A row order that settles the question is what a Reformed or Baptist reader will object to, and a note cannot undo it.
fixes.fix: Split into two rows, side by side, neither first: ‘Everyone, all, the world’ (Isa 45:22, John 3:17, Rom 11:26, 1 Tim 2:4, Titus 2:11, 1 John 4:14) and ‘A few, the remnant, the chosen’ (Matt 24:22, Mark 13:20, Rom 9:27, 2 Thess 2:13, 2 Tim 2:10). This takes the count to 32; see the merges below.

fixes.row: Asked and answered: “Who then can be saved?” … “Unless you are circumcised”
fixes.why: The label quotes ‘Unless you are circumcised’ and none of the four examples shows it (rule 6). Inside ‘what the text says to do’, the Judean teaching reads as one more recipe, and a rabbi may hear the circumcision verse set up as the wrong answer. The note already names Acts 15:1 and 15:11, so the verse does not need to sit in the list.
fixes.fix: Remove ‘Unless you are circumcised’ from the label and Acts.15.1 from this row’s verses. Keep the question and the answer (Acts 15:1 and 15:11) in the note only, quoted in full.

fixes.why: ‘The earliest manuscripts lack’ is repeated under this row, ‘Said as still to come’ and ‘Asked and answered’, so Mark 16:16 is marked three times as doubtful. The Baptist, Pentecostal, Catholic and Orthodox readers hold the longer ending as Scripture, and will read the repetition as the page taking a side against a verse they hold. The textual fact belongs once, in neutral terms, in the marking the site already uses for Mark 16:9-20.
fixes.fix: Keep one note, in this row, in the site’s standing marking for Mark 16:9-20. Delete the same sentence from ‘Said as still to come’ and from ‘Asked and answered’.

fixes.row: Saved, and faith, believing, trust, refuge
fixes.why: Matt 27:42 is the mockers’ ‘He saved others; He cannot save Himself’. Its faith word is their mocking ‘we will believe in Him’. Under a faith row it reads as a faith statement, and it is already in the cross row.
fixes.fix: Remove Matt.27.42 from this row’s verses. It stays in ‘He saved others; He cannot save Himself’.

fixes.row: Rock, light, strength, song, horn, shield, storehouse, helmet, garments, adorned, cup, walls, wells
fixes.why: Six of the thirteen items (garments, adorned, cup, walls, wells, storehouse) have no example. The four examples show strength, light, helmet and the horn, so the label claims more than the examples show (rule 6).
fixes.fix: Give each unshown item one example from this row’s verses: Isa 61:10 for garments and adorned, Ps 116:13 for cup, Isa 26:1 for walls, Isa 12:3 for wells; storehouse only if the Berean reads it so in Isa 33:6. Or cut the label to the items shown.

fixes.row: Salvation, and works, obedience, repentance, the commandments: worked out, inherited, obtained, neglected
fixes.why: Acts 5:31 calls Christ ‘Prince and Savior’, the title, not the word for salvation, and it belongs with ‘Jesus called Savior’. Ps 119:155 (‘salvation is far from the wicked’) is in this row and in ‘No salvation’, so it is read twice, and this row’s label reads it as obedience.
fixes.fix: Move Acts.5.31 to ‘Jesus called Savior; salvation in Christ’. Remove Ps.119.155 from this row; it stays under ‘No salvation … salvation is far’.

fixes.why: Four verses here also stand in other rows: 2 Sam 10:11 and 1 Chr 19:12 in ‘A person saves … a rescuer’; Acts 4:12 in ‘Saved by … no other name’; 1 Tim 4:10 in ‘Who is saved’. The catch-all is the wrong place for Acts 4:12, the exclusive-name verse, since a reader sees it set aside as a leftover.
fixes.fix: Remove these four from ‘Every other use’. The catch-all keeps only verses that stand in no other row.

fixes.why: This row and ‘Saved from sins, wrath, death, uncleanness’ both say saved from death, the soul, the life. James 5:20 stands in both. Four verses do not make a row of their own.
fixes.fix: Merge into ‘Saved from sins, wrath, death, uncleanness, a life, a soul’. Keep Matt 16:25 and Mark 3:4 as examples of ‘save a life’ in the same row. Do not merge into the rescuers row: these verses are not about a person who rescues.

fixes.row: God and salvation: “the salvation of the LORD”, “the God of my salvation”, “God our Savior”
fixes.why: ‘Salvation is the LORD’s’ and this row both say the salvation is God’s. Rev 7:10 stands in both, and its note is in one. Two rows for one claim.
fixes.fix: Merge ‘Salvation is the LORD’s’ into this row, keep Rev.7.10 once, and keep its note.

fixes.why: The note gives the Berean’s reading of Jude 5 (‘Jesus had delivered His people’). The worker’s report records that other manuscripts read ‘the Lord’. The note does not say so, and a reader who knows the other reading is left to find it.
fixes.fix: Add to the note that some manuscripts read ‘the Lord’ in this verse. Checked against the worker’s report, not against the manuscripts.

fixes.row: Salvation, and works, obedience, repentance (noun form) and Saved, and works, deeds (verb form)
fixes.why: Faith and works is the pair the two sides argue from. The note names Eph 2:9-10 only, and Eph 2:9 (‘not by works’) is quoted only there. The James and Romans verses on justification by works and faith are not on the page, and neither has the word ‘saved’, so neither side’s key verse is shown.
fixes.fix: See missing 1: name Jas 2:24 and Rom 3:28 in the note, one for each side, as the worker did for Eph 2:9-10.

worker_points.point: 1. Whether salvation can be lost (rows 17 and 18)
worker_points.why: The split follows the verb’s tense, and both sides’ key verses are named in the note (John 10:28, Heb 6:6). 1 Cor 15:2 stands in both rows because its verb has both tenses; that is correct.

worker_points.point: 2. Election and choice; who is saved (row 20)
worker_points.why: The label puts the universal side first. Split into two rows (fix 1).
The uneven count is not itself a tilt, since Eph 2:9-10 hold no word for saved. The gap is that the sides’ key justification verses are missing (missing 1).
Two verses is a fair size for a row that has ‘saved’ and ‘baptism’ in the same verse. The problem is the repeated Mark 16:9-20 note (fix 3).
The circumcision quote in the label has no example and reads as a recipe (fix 2).
Each row holds verses that name the speaker, or quote the speaker’s own ‘I’. Acts 4:12 belongs in ‘no other name’ (row 6); its duplicate in the catch-all is fix 7.
The label is the mockers’ words and the note says whose words they are. This is the neutral form.
The note says the same Greek word and that the page does not say which is meant. No tilt for the Pentecostal or Catholic reader.
Most verses are rescue and victory in battle, shown as the Hebrew has them. Zech 9:9 is not assigned a referent and the note says so.
Stands in two rows, both saying the salvation is God’s (fix 9).

worker_points.point: 11. Hard verses kept (Judg 10:13, Hab 1:2, Jer 14:9, Ps 22:1, Ps 3:2, Isa 59:11)
worker_points.why: Keeping the complaints where they are said is the rule. Ps 22:1 needs a pointer to the cross (missing 2), not a move.

missing.what: Jas 2:24 (‘justified by works and not by faith alone’) and Rom 3:28 (‘justified by faith apart from works’) are the verses the two sides of faith and works argue from. Neither has the word ‘saved’, so the hub does not show them. Name both in the faith and works note, one for each side, as the worker did for Eph 2:9-10.

Ps 22:1 sits under ‘No salvation’ with ‘so far from saving me’. The Gospels give the same opening line as Jesus’ cry on the cross (Matt 27:46; Mark 15:34). The row does not link them, and a Christian reader will look for the link. A pointer in the note, with no verdict, is enough.

examples_checked: 22 of 31 labelled rows show every item of their label among their four examples. Rows 2, 6, 8, 19, 20, 24, 26, 30 and 31 do not (fixes 2, 4, 5 and the missing items). Checked against the Berean text stored in the built hub, not re-fetched verse by verse.
summary: The hub is faithful to the text and its notes say where the traditions part, so it can ship once the fixes are made. The label order in ‘Who is saved’ and the repeated Mark 16:16 note are the two places where a reader in one of the traditions would be pushed toward a side.
